thesis: The speaker recounts his career beginning at age 15 when he traded P. Lard cigarettes instead of AT&T, making $26 on a single trade and deciding then that he wanted to be in the stock market. He describes his early education in geography and history while studying the market daily, followed by a period teaching school and attending law school before becoming a retail broker. His first major success came in 1972 with a recommendation for Houston oil and gas, which rose from 10 to 110 due to a massive gas discovery in unregulated state waters.
